newsitem.title: POLAND: BWR to buy back own shares on bourse.
newsitem.headline: BWR to buy back own shares on bourse.

text.p: Poland's Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej SA (BWR) will buy back its own shares on the Warsaw bourse to take over Bank Secesyjny SA, BWR's spokesman said on Monday.
Franciszek Palowski told Reuters BWR, which wanted to give 25 of its own shares for each of Bank Secesyjny shares to Secesyjny's shareholders, would issue new stock for that purpose.

"The merger of Bank Secesyjny and BWR will take place without BWR's capital rise," Palowski said. "This would mean, that we have to get the shares on the market, namely, buy them back from the market," he said.
On December 10 shareholders of Bank Secesyjny SA approved the merger with BWR and shareholders of BWR are expected to vote on the issue on December 23.
BWR, which has a 34.9 percent stake, has been implementing a financial restructuring programme in Secesyjny for the last two years under an agreement with the central bank.
Other shareholders of Secesyjny include the Katowice steel mill with 30.2 percent, a coal trading agency with 26.7 percent as well as other steel mill and coal agencies.
Its capital is 9,964,500 zlotys divided into 99,645 shares.
BWR's capital is 31,255,205 zlotys divided into 12,502,802 shares. BWR's net after 10 months of 1996 was 4.1 million zlotys against 2.4 million in the same period last year.
